title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
hints: Use a hash map to store the complement of each element.
For each number, check if target - num exists in the map.
solution_approach: Iterate through the array. For each element, calculate complement = target - current. If complement exists in hash map, return both indices. Otherwise, store current element with its index in the map.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and a different day in the future to sell that stock. Return the maximum profit. If no profit is possible, return 0.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price=1), sell on day 5 (price=6), profit = 5

hints: Track the minimum price seen so far.
At each step, calculate profit if sold today.
solution_approach: Keep track of minimum price. At each day, calculate potential profit (current - min). Update max profit. Time O(n), Space O(1).

sample_code.python:
def max_profit(prices):
    min_price = float('inf')
    max_profit = 0
    for p in prices:
        min_price = min(min_price, p)
        max_profit = max(max_profit, p - min_price)
    return max_profit

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum. A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6

hints: Use Kadane's algorithm.
At each position, decide: extend the current subarray or start fresh.
solution_approach: Kadane's algorithm: maintain current_sum. At each element, current_sum = max(nums[i], current_sum + nums[i]). Track global max. Time O(n).

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i]. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.

examples.explanation: Each element is product of all others
Zero in array means products with that index are 0

hints: Compute prefix products and suffix products separately.
Use two passes: left-to-right and right-to-left.
solution_approach: First pass: build prefix products left to right. Second pass: multiply by suffix products right to left. O(n) time, O(1) extra space (output array doesn't count).

sample_code.python:
def product_except_self(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    result = [1] * n
    left = 1
    for i in range(n):
        result[i] = left
        left *= nums[i]
    right = 1
    for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
        result[i] *= right
        right *= nums[i]
    return result

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

examples.explanation: Intervals [1,4] and [4,5] are adjacent, merged to [1,5]

hints: Sort intervals by start time first.
Compare each interval's start with the previous interval's end.
solution_approach: Sort by start time. Iterate and merge: if current start <= previous end, extend previous end. Otherwise, add new interval. O(n log n) time.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise. An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
hints: Count character frequencies.
Compare the frequency counts.
solution_approach: Count characters in both strings using a fixed-size array (26 for lowercase). Compare counts. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within the string.
hints: Use a sliding window approach.
Track the last seen position of each character.
solution_approach: Sliding window with hash map storing last index of each character. When duplicate found, move left pointer past previous occurrence. O(n) time.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order. An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word.

examples.explanation: Empty string forms its own group

hints: Use the sorted version of each string as a key.
Group strings by their sorted key in a hash map.
solution_approach: For each string, sort it to create a key. Use a hash map to group strings with the same sorted key. O(n * k log k) where k is max string length.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s. A palindrome reads the same backward as forward.

examples.explanation: Both are valid longest palindromic substrings

hints: Expand around each possible center.
A palindrome has a center - either a single character or between two characters.
solution_approach: For each index, expand outward treating it as center. Handle both odd-length (single center) and even-length (two centers) palindromes. O(n^2) time, O(1) space.

title: Palindrome Number
description: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome integer. An integer is a palindrome when it reads the same backward as forward. For example, 121 is a palindrome while 123 is not.

examples.explanation: Reads as 121- backward, not a palindrome

hints: Negative numbers are never palindromes.
Convert to string or reverse the number mathematically.
solution_approach: Negative numbers return false. Convert to string and compare with its reverse. Or reverse the number mathematically and compare. O(log n) time.

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list. Implement iteratively and recursively.
hints: Use three pointers: prev, current, next.
Iteratively reverse each node's next pointer.
solution_approach: Iterative: maintain prev, current, next. For each node, reverse its next pointer to prev. Move all three forward. O(n) time, O(1) space.

sample_code.python:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    return prev

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.

examples.explanation: One empty list, one with single element

hints: Use a dummy head node to simplify edge cases.
Compare heads and attach the smaller node.
solution_approach: Use a dummy node. Compare heads of both lists, attach smaller to result. Move that pointer forward. Attach remaining. O(n+m) time.

title: Linked List Cycle
description: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it. There is a cycle if some node in the list can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer.

examples.explanation: Tail connects to node at index 1
No cycle, pos=-1 means no cycle

hints: Use Floyd's tortoise and hare algorithm.
Use two pointers, one moving 1 step and another 2 steps.
solution_approach: Floyd's cycle detection: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. If they meet, there's a cycle. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head. Do this in one pass.

examples.explanation: Removed the 2nd node from end (node with value 4)

hints: Use a two-pointer approach with a gap of n.
Use a dummy node to handle edge cases.
solution_approach: Move first pointer n steps ahead. Then move both pointers until first reaches end. Second pointer is just before the node to remove. O(n) time, one pass.

title: Add Two Numbers
description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each node contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list.
hints: Traverse both lists simultaneously.
Keep a carry variable for sums >= 10.
solution_approach: Add corresponding digits with carry. Create new nodes for each digit. Handle remaining carry at the end. O(max(n,m)) time.

sample_code.python:
def add_two_numbers(l1, l2):
    dummy = node = ListNode(0)
    carry = 0
    while l1 or l2 or carry:
        v1 = l1.val if l1 else 0
        v2 = l2.val if l2 else 0
        carry, val = divmod(v1 + v2 + carry, 10)
        node.next = ListNode(val)
        node = node.next
        l1 = l1.next if l1 else None
        l2 = l2.next if l2 else None
    return dummy.next

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.
hints: Use recursion: depth = max(left_depth, right_depth) + 1.
Base case: empty tree has depth 0.
solution_approach: Recursive DFS: return 1 + max(maxDepth(left), maxDepth(right)). Base case: None returns 0. O(n) time, O(h) space where h is height.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST is defined as: the left subtree contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key, the right subtree contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key, and both subtrees must also be valid BSTs.

examples.explanation: Node 4 is in the left subtree of 5 but 4 < 5 is ok, however 3 is in right subtree of 4 but 3 < 4

hints: Pass down min and max constraints.
Each node must be within a valid range.
solution_approach: DFS with min/max bounds. For left child, max becomes parent value. For right child, min becomes parent value. O(n) time.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values. Level order traversal visits nodes level by level from left to right.
hints: Use BFS with a queue.
Process all nodes at current level before moving to next.
solution_approach: BFS using queue. For each level, record the size, process that many nodes, enqueue their children. O(n) time.

title: Invert Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root. Inverting means swapping left and right children of every node.

examples.explanation: Every left and right child swapped

hints: Use recursion: swap left and right, then recurse.
Or use BFS/DFS iteratively.
solution_approach: Recursive: swap root.left and root.right, then invert both subtrees. O(n) time.

sample_code.python:
def invert_tree(root):
    if not root:
        return None
    root.left, root.right = root.right, root.left
    invert_tree(root.left)
    invert_tree(root.right)
    return root

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes p and q. The LCA is the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node can be a descendant of itself).

examples.explanation: 5 is ancestor of 4, so LCA is 5

hints: If current node is None, p, or q, return it.
Recurse left and right; if both return non-None, current is LCA.
solution_approach: Recursive post-order. If root is p or q, return root. Recurse left and right. If both return, root is LCA. If only one returns, propagate that. O(n) time.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.
hints: Use DFS or BFS to flood-fill each island.
Mark visited cells to avoid counting twice.
solution_approach: Iterate through grid. When '1' found, increment count and DFS/BFS to mark all connected '1's as visited. O(m*n) time.

title: Clone Graph
description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph. Each node contains a value and a list of its neighbors.
hints: Use a hash map to track cloned nodes.
DFS or BFS, creating clones as you visit.
solution_approach: DFS with visited map. For each node, if not cloned, create clone and recurse on neighbors. O(V+E) time.

title: Course Schedule
description: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take, labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [ai, bi] indicates that you must take course bi before course ai. Return true if you can finish all courses (detect cycle).
hints: This is a cycle detection problem in a directed graph.
Use topological sort (Kahn's algorithm) or DFS with states.
solution_approach: Kahn's algorithm (BFS topological sort): compute in-degrees, process nodes with 0 in-degree, reduce neighbors' in-degrees. If all processed, no cycle. O(V+E) time.

sample_code.python:
from collections import deque

def can_finish(num, prereqs):
    adj = [[] for _ in range(num)]
    indeg = [0] * num
    for a, b in prereqs:
        adj[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    queue = deque([i for i in range(num) if indeg[i] == 0])
    count = 0
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        count += 1
        for nei in adj[node]:
            indeg[nei] -= 1
            if indeg[nei] == 0:
                queue.append(nei)
    return count == num

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description: Given an m x n matrix of heights, where each cell represents the height of terrain, water flows from a cell to an adjacent cell with equal or lower height. Determine the list of cells where water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.

examples.explanation: These cells can reach both oceans

hints: Reverse the problem: start from ocean cells and flow backwards (uphill).
Use DFS from Pacific border and Atlantic border, then find intersection.
solution_approach: DFS from all Pacific-border cells and all Atlantic-border cells. Mark reachable cells. Intersection of both sets is the answer. O(m*n) time.

title: Graph Valid Tree
description: Given n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges, write a function to check whether these edges form a valid tree. A valid tree is connected and has no cycles.
hints: A tree with n nodes has exactly n-1 edges.
Check connectivity AND no cycles using Union-Find or DFS.
solution_approach: Union-Find: process edges, if two nodes already connected, cycle exists. After all edges, check all nodes are connected. O(E * α(N)) time.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hints: This is the Fibonacci sequence in disguise.
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).
solution_approach: DP: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Base: dp[1]=1, dp[2]=2. Or use two variables. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Coin Change
description: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return -1.
hints: Build up from 0 to amount.
For each amount, try all coins and take the minimum.
solution_approach: Bottom-up DP. dp[i] = min coins for amount i. For each i, try each coin: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin]+1). O(amount * coins) time.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence is a sequence derived from an array by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.
hints: DP approach: dp[i] = length of LIS ending at index i.
Binary search approach: maintain a sorted tails array.
solution_approach: DP: for each i, check all j < i and update dp[i] = max(dp[j]+1) if nums[j] < nums[i]. O(n^2). Or use patience sorting with binary search for O(n log n).

title: House Robber
description: You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed. The only constraint stopping you from robbing each of them is that adjacent houses have security systems connected. If two adjacent houses were broken into on the same night, the police are alerted. Given an array nums representing the amount of money at each house, return the maximum amount you can rob without alerting the police.
hints: At each house, choose: rob it (add to previous-previous max) or skip it (take previous max).
dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).
solution_approach: DP with two variables. At each step: skip = max_so_far, rob = prev_max + current. Update prev_max and max_so_far. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
description: Given n items, each with a weight and a value, determine the maximum value that can be obtained by putting items in a knapsack of capacity W. You can either take or leave each item (0/1 choice).
hints: Build a 2D DP table: dp[i][w] = max value using first i items with capacity w.
For each item, choose: include it or exclude it.
solution_approach: 2D DP: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w-weight[i]] + value[i]). Space-optimized to 1D. O(n*W) time.

title: Merge Sort
description: Implement the merge sort algorithm. Given an array of integers, sort it in ascending order using the merge sort technique. Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm.
hints: Split array in half recursively until single elements.
Merge two sorted halves back together.
solution_approach: Divide: split array in half. Conquer: recursively sort halves. Combine: merge two sorted arrays. O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

title: Binary Search
description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index if the target is found. If not, return -1. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
hints: Compare target with middle element.
Eliminate half the array each step.
solution_approach: Standard binary search: maintain left and right pointers. Compare mid with target, move left or right accordingly. O(log n) time.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted array that has been rotated at some pivot unknown to you beforehand, and a target value, return the index if found or -1. You must find it in O(log n) time.
hints: One half is always sorted.
Determine which half is sorted, then check if target lies in that range.
solution_approach: Modified binary search. At each step, determine which half is sorted. If target is in sorted half, search there; otherwise search the other half. O(log n).

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Given the rotated array, return the minimum element. You must find it in O(log n) time.
hints: Compare mid with the rightmost element.
If mid > right, minimum is in the right half; otherwise left half.
solution_approach: Binary search comparing mid with right boundary. If nums[mid] > nums[right], pivot is in right half. Otherwise, left half. O(log n).

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array. Note that it is the kth largest element in the sorted order, not the kth distinct element.
hints: Sort and pick the kth from the end.
Or use a min-heap of size k.
Or use quickselect.
solution_approach: Min-heap approach: maintain a heap of size k. For each element, if heap size < k, push; else if element > heap min, replace. O(n log k) time.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of brackets and in the correct order.
hints: Use a stack to track opening brackets.
When closing bracket found, check if top of stack is matching opening bracket.
solution_approach: Push opening brackets onto stack. For closing brackets, check if stack top matches. Stack must be empty at end. O(n) time.

title: Min Stack
description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time. Implement the MinStack class with O(1) time complexity for all operations.

examples.input: push(-2), push(0), push(-3), getMin(), pop(), top(), getMin()
examples.explanation: getMin returns -3, after pop top is 0, getMin returns -2

examples.input: push(1), push(2), top(), getMin(), pop(), getMin()

hints: Use two stacks: one for values, one for minimums.
Or store (value, current_min) pairs in a single stack.
solution_approach: Maintain a parallel min-stack. When pushing, also push current min. When popping, pop both. O(1) for all operations.

title: Implement Queue using Stacks
description: Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks. The implemented queue should support all the functions of a normal queue: push, peek, pop, and empty.

examples.explanation: Peek returns front (1), pop returns 1, not empty

examples.input: push(1), push(2), push(3), peek(), pop(), pop()

hints: Use two stacks: one for input, one for output.
When output stack is empty, transfer all from input stack.
solution_approach: Amortized O(1): push to input stack. When output empty, pop all from input to output (reverses order). Pop/peek from output. O(1) amortized.

title: Daily Temperatures
description: Given an array of integers temperatures represents the daily temperatures, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after the ith day to get a warmer temperature. If there is no future day for which this is possible, keep answer[i] == 0.

examples.explanation: Day 0 waits 1 day for 74, day 2 waits 4 days for 76, etc.
Each day waits 1 day for warmer

hints: Use a monotonic decreasing stack.
Store indices in the stack, compare temperatures.
solution_approach: Monotonic stack: iterate temperatures. While stack top has lower temp, pop and calculate distance. Push current index. O(n) time.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. Return the max value in each window position.
hints: Use a monotonic decreasing deque.
Remove elements that are smaller than current from the back.
solution_approach: Monotonic deque storing indices. Remove from back if smaller than current. Remove from front if out of window. Front is always max. O(n) time.

title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.
hints: Use a set to track seen elements.
If element already in set, duplicate found.
solution_approach: Hash set: iterate and add elements. If element already in set, return True. O(n) time, O(n) space.

sample_code.python:
def contains_duplicate(nums):
    return len(nums) != len(set(nums))

title: Roman to Integer
description: Given a roman numeral, convert it to an integer. Roman numerals are represented by seven different symbols: I, V, X, L, C, D, M. If a smaller symbol appears before a larger one, it is subtracted.
hints: Map each symbol to its value.
If current value is less than next value, subtract it.
solution_approach: Right to left iteration. If current value >= next, add; else subtract. O(n) time.

title: LRU Cache
description: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Implement the LRUCache class with get and put methods, both in O(1) average time complexity.

examples.input: LRUCache(2), put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), put(3,3), get(2)
examples.explanation: get(1) returns 1. put(3,3) evicts key 2. get(2) returns -1

hints: Combine a hash map with a doubly linked list.
Hash map for O(1) lookup, linked list for O(1) reordering.
solution_approach: HashMap stores key -> node. Doubly linked list maintains order (most recent at head). Get: move to head, return value. Put: add to head, evict from tail if full. O(1) both.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order. The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
hints: Count frequencies with a hash map.
Use a bucket sort approach or a heap.
solution_approach: Count frequencies. Bucket sort: create buckets indexed by frequency. Collect top k from high to low buckets. O(n) time.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time.
hints: Use a hash set for O(1) lookups.
Only start counting from the beginning of a sequence (num-1 not in set).
solution_approach: Hash set. For each number, if num-1 is not in set, it's the start of a sequence. Count consecutive from there. O(n) time.

title: Jump Game
description: Given an integer array nums, you are initially positioned at the first index. Each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position. Determine if you are able to reach the last index.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step to index 1, then 3 steps to last
You will always be stuck at index 3 (value 0)

hints: Track the farthest reachable index.
If current index exceeds farthest, you're stuck.
solution_approach: Greedy: maintain max_reach. At each index, if i > max_reach, return False. Update max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). O(n) time.

title: Activity Selection / Non-overlapping Intervals
description: Given a collection of intervals, find the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest non-overlapping.
hints: Sort intervals by end time.
Greedy: always keep the interval that ends earliest.
solution_approach: Sort by end time. Count how many we can keep without overlap. Answer = total - count. O(n log n) time.

title: Partition Labels
description: You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
hints: First, record the last occurrence of each character.
Expand the current partition end to the last occurrence of each char seen.
solution_approach: Record last index of each char. Iterate string, expanding partition end to max last occurrence. When i reaches partition end, cut. O(n) time.
